title: Multimodal Augmentation and Transferability Playbook for Quantized Deployments
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary

Purpose: This playbook documents a prescriptive, reproducible approach to generate multimodal probe sets and augmented synthetic traffic that reveal transferability risks for quantized model artifacts. It focuses on image+text and audio+text use cases for inference deployments (hosted, Dedicated, Private) and integrates with Redwood's eval-harness and quantization profiles.

Why this exists
- Quantization and kernel optimizations can interact with non-text inputs in subtle ways (tokenization boundary shift, preprocessing mismatch, per-modality clipping) that are not captured by text-only probes.
- Multimodal augmentation exposes brittle feature transforms and distribution gaps before rollout to Dedicated or Private fleets.
- This playbook enables consistent signal for promotion gates and regression triage.

Scope and audience
- Audience: ML engineers, applied-researchers, SREs responsible for model promotion and private deployments.
- Scope: Probe generation, augmentation transforms, evaluation metrics, CI integration, rollout gating, and triage steps. Not covered: low-level kernel tuning (see runtime team docs) or legal/privacy policies for third-party data.

High-level approach
1) Start from a representative seed set: small curated multimodal examples for each supported modality and intent slice (e.g., OCR-like text-in-image, visual question-answering, audio command with background noise). Seed size: 150–500 examples per slice.
2) Apply deterministic and stochastic augmentations in layered passes to simulate field variability (preprocessor shifts, compression, timing jitter, overlay noise).
3) Run deterministic replays in the eval-harness to record metric deltas against a baseline (float32 reference) and against the previously promoted artifact.
4) Synthesize transferability reports that quantify degradation per-slice and recommend rollback or mitigation (quant fallback, higher-precision kernels, alternative preprocessors).

Augmentation catalogue (recommended transforms)
- Image transforms:
  - JPEG compression levels: 95, 80, 60, 40 (simulate mobile uploads and thumbnails).
  - Color-space perturbation: small gamma shifts (+/- 0.2), convert to grayscale and back.
  - Cropping and aspect-ratio drift: central crop 0.85–0.98, random resize padding.
  - Overlay occlusions: 10–30% area with solid or patterned mask.
  - Synthetic text overlay: add rendered text at random positions (font variations).
- Audio transforms:
  - Background SNR levels: +20dB, +10dB, +5dB, 0dB (mix with office noise, street noise).
  - Codec compression: low-bitrate AAC/Opus profiles and resampling to 16kHz/8kHz.
  - Temporal jitter: insert 50–300ms gaps and stretch/compress by +/-5%.
- Text transforms (context for multimodal tasks):
  - Tokenization boundary noise: insert zero-width spaces, soft hyphenation, mixed Unicode normalizations (NFC vs NFD).
  - Paraphrase augmentation: 1–2 token-level paraphrases preserving intent.
  - Prompt scaffold changes: switch instruction framing (imperative->question) and add irrelevant metadata fields.

Transform orchestration model
- Layered passes: deterministic pass (all transforms applied at fixed parameters) followed by stochastic pass (randomly sampled transforms seeded from PR ID).
- Multiplicative blow-up: cap augmented outputs at 12x seeds for CI-level coverage; larger offline batches (50–100x) for full stress runs.
- Keep provenance: embed a canonical augmentation header into each probe record: "augment-chain: jpeg80|gamma+0.1|overlay-id:7"

Metrics and acceptance criteria
- Core metrics to record (per-slice):
  - Semantic Accuracy (task-specific, e.g., VQA exact match or top-1 intent accuracy)
  - Embedding Cosine Drop: median and 95th percentile cosine distance to float baseline embedding for same input
  - Response Stability Index (RSI): Jaccard token overlap and normalized log-prob delta aggregated over n-best outputs
  - Latency delta: p50/p95 delta under quantized artifact vs float baseline
  - Failure modes: OOMs, invalid tokens, preprocessor exceptions

Acceptance table (example thresholds used for promotion gating)
| metric | allowed delta vs float32 | action if exceeded |
| Semantic Accuracy | > 1.5% absolute drop (slice-level) | block promotion; investigate preprocessing mismatch |
| Median Embedding Cosine Drop | > 0.04 | run embedding recalibration / tighter tokenization |
| RSI (95th) | > 0.25 | triage for hallucination and top-k instability |
| Latency p95 | +35% | consider lighter quant profile or batching tuning |
| OOMs or preprocessor errors | any occurrence | immediate rollback candidate |

Integrations with Redwood systems
- Eval-harness: implement an augmentation runner component that ports augmented probes into the existing job schema. Use the existing evaluator job tags: probe.type=multimodal, probe.augment.version=<semver>.
- Quantization profiles: store per-profile guardrails that reference augmentation-sensitive slices (e.g., "image-ocr") so automated rollback logic can trigger quant-fallback to float16 or int8-consistent kernels.
- Telemetry: tag telemetry with augment-chain and model_artifact_id for traceability in Console dashboards.

CI / Pipeline recipe (recommended)
1) Pull candidate model artifact and float32 baseline artifact.
2) Trigger lightweight augmented smoke with 12x seeds against a fast path quant profile (runtime can use reduced sequence lengths).
3) If any slice fails acceptance table, run targeted 100x stress on affected slices and notify on-call eval team.
4) If stress confirms failure, the artifact is flagged for quant rollback or re-quantize with adjusted calibration data.

CLI examples
- Generate an augmented batch (local dev):
  rwood-evalctl generate --seed-file seeds/vqa-seed.jsonl --augment-profile multimodal-basic --out probes/aug-vqa.jsonl
- Run smoke eval against an artifact (using eval-harness):
  rwood-evalctl run --artifact-id rwd-model:v2-quant --baseline rwd-model:v2-fp32 --probes probes/aug-vqa.jsonl --report out/reports/vqa-augment-smoke.json

Probe record format (text line example)
- Each line is newline-delimited JSON in the eval-harness format. Include these top-level keys (flat): id, seed_id, augment_chain, modality, input_uri, expected_label, slice, timestamp. Example: {"id":"p-000234","seed_id":"s-112","augment_chain":"jpeg80|gamma+0.1|overlay-7","modality":"image+text","input_uri":"gs://probe-bucket/images/ocr/0012.png","expected_label":"Invoice 4723","slice":"ocr-invoice","timestamp":"2026-01-08T14:22:00Z"}

Triage and debugging playbook (fast path)
1) Reproduce: run the failing probe(s) against float baseline and candidate in isolation. Confirm delta.
2) Isolate transform: remove augmentation layers iteratively to find minimal failing chain.
3) Inspect preprocessing: compare image decoding libraries, color space conversion, tokenization byte-level outputs.
4) Check quant artifacts: re-run quantized runtime with logging of kernel selection and kv-cache behavior (trace id in telemetry).
5) Mitigations:
   - Short-term: quant-fallback on the affected slice via rollout policy (use canary with traffic partition).
   - Medium-term: add targeted calibration data for augmentations and re-run post-training quantization or mixed-precision re-quantization.
   - Long-term: expand core probes to include the discovered failure mode and automate the guardrail for subsequent promotions.

Operational considerations and cost
- Cost: augmented suites blow up probe counts; use tiered runs (smoke 12x on PRs, stress 100x nightly for candidate artifacts).
- Storage: keep only provenance headers and a sample shard for long-term storage (retain full augmented dataset for 90 days unless flagged).
- Privacy: strip PII before augmentation or use synthetic placeholders; if customer data is required, run in Private deployment with appropriate consent and KMS controls.

Ownership and escalation
- Owners: Applied ML (primary) — Maya Chen; Runtime team (secondary) — Jordan Kline.
- On-call escalation: open a ticket to #eval-oncall and notify runtime-sre if the triage points to kernel-level regressions.

Appendices
A. Sample augmentation YAML (eval-harness friendly)
augment-profile: multimodal-basic
seed-glob: "seeds/*-vqa.jsonl"
passes:
  - name: deterministic
    transforms:
      - jpeg_compress: 80
      - gamma_shift: 0.1
  - name: stochastic
    transforms:
      - random_overlay: {prob: 0.35, max_area: 0.25}
      - token_boundary_noise: {prob: 0.2}
out_format: eval-harness-jsonl

B. Quick checklist for promotability
- Smoke pass completed within acceptance thresholds
- Stress pass has no new failure modes or OOMs
- Augment provenance attached to telemetry and Console dashboards
- Calibration plan exists if embedding drift or RSI exceed soft thresholds
